:::{#def-interaction}
#### Interaction and interaction term

Consider a regression model whose linear predictor $\eta(\vx)$
includes two covariates $x_j$ and $x_k$.
The model includes an **interaction** between $x_j$ and $x_k$
when the difference in $\eta(\vx)$ per unit difference in $x_j$,
holding the other covariates fixed,
depends on the value of $x_k$.

An **interaction term** is a term in the linear predictor
formed by multiplying two (or more) covariates together,
such as $\b_{jk} x_j x_k$;
its coefficient $\b_{jk}$ is called an **interaction coefficient**.
A linear predictor with two covariates and their interaction term has the form:

$$
\eta(\vx) \eqdef \b_0 + \b_j x_j + \b_k x_k + \b_{jk} x_j x_k
$$

:::

::: notes
@def-interaction describes only how the linear predictor varies across subpopulations,
so it makes no causal claim.
Interaction is also scale-dependent:
@def-interaction is stated on the scale of the linear predictor $\eta(\vx)$,
which can differ from the scale of the mean $\mu(\vx)$.
:::
